clue.text: Bananas split best from the end

parts.note: a split or fissure

indicators.note: reading a word starting from its end means taking its letters backwards

parts.note: the best is the top

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe: a banana split is best eaten starting from the far end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas split' reads as the dessert, but 'Bananas' is the definition and 'split' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is informal for crazy, and a crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person, so both describe someone mad.

clue.text: Strange people full of one thought

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it within, so these words wrap around the single letter

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a people, as a nation
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An odd tribe obsessed with one single idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is old British slang for odd; the numeral sits between the two halves of the outer phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumination is deep, prolonged pondering, which makes it a fair synonym for a thought or for thinking.

clue.text: Loud noise making bottom hot in lesson

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the final letter, and this asks for it to be swapped for the hot abbreviation

parts.note: a lesson at school is a class
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A noisy classroom where someone gets a smacked, stinging bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S of CLASS, its bottom in a down light, becomes H.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash is the harsh ringing sound of metal objects striking, such as cymbals, so a loud noise.

clue.text: Show a little light on one side of ship?

indicators.note: in a down entry, one item placed on another sits above it, so the side of the ship comes first

parts.note: port is the left side of a vessel
a ray is a thin beam of light

explanation.surface: Displaying a small lamp on the side of a boat, as navigation rules require.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the ship's lights are a red herring; the pieces are the side and the beam.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent something, as an artist or actor does when they show it.

clue.text: New telethon begins, time to react to poverty

indicators.note: something new is freshly made, so the following letters are made into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A charity telethon starts up, a timely response to poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the telethon the reaction to poverty; really the response is personal belt-tightening.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten one's belt is an idiom for spending less and economising when money is short.

clue.text: Just small hint

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to hint is to imply

explanation.surface: Nothing more than a tiny suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Simply and just both mean merely or only, as in 'it was just a joke'.

clue.text: Popular quartet back in concert after quiet rest day

indicators.note: the band and the closing letter follow the word for silence in the order of the entry

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
the hugely popular Swedish pop foursome

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pop group performs after a quiet day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in concert' looks like the band playing live, but 'back in concert' just keeps the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabbat is the Hebrew name for the Jewish Sabbath, the weekly day of rest from Friday evening to Saturday evening.

clue.text: With holes made in the cupboard, possibly test temperature inside for hens

definitions.text: With holes made in the cupboard, possibly

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars
heat as a measure of temperature

indicators.note: the inside of a word is what lies between its ends, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: Checking the warmth inside a henhouse, while something has chewed holes in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temperature inside' tempts a T placed inside something; instead heat is the word and 'inside' takes the centre of 'hens'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes left in a wardrobe can be holed by moth larvae, and such damaged fabric is described as moth-eaten.

clue.text: See, nearly see, no longer see?

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddling chant about sight fading away word by word.
explanation.walkthrough: The three 'see's play different roles: an archaic synonym, a word to be cut short, and part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose something, or lose sight of it, means you can no longer see it, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Spoil one's partner

parts.note: one is means I am, contracted to I'm
to partner is to pair with someone

explanation.surface: Pampering one's spouse too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' reads as a possessive but stands for 'one is', which is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to damage or weaken something, which is what spoiling it does.

clue.text: Large lady sings at the end of Salome broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so just that one is kept

parts.note: last letter of the opera's title

explanation.surface: A big soprano performs in the finale of Strauss's opera Salome on air, the 'fat lady singing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A giantess is a female giant, so a woman of enormous size.

clue.text: Stingy tea hosted by university board

indicators.note: a host takes a guest inside their home, so these outer words take in the drink

parts.note: uni is short for university
char is British slang for tea
a board, as a table at mealtimes

explanation.surface: A mean little tea party laid on by the university's governors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' reads as governing body but means a table; tea in British slang is char.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncharitable means ungenerous or mean-spirited, and stingy describes the same lack of generosity, here in judgement.

clue.text: Member of the team keeps tardy worker on track

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the team word holds the other inside

parts.note: a team member is a player
tardy means late

explanation.surface: A team player covers for a slacker so the project stays on track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on track' sounds like keeping a job on schedule; it means railway track. LATE sits inside P-AYER.
explanation.definitionFit: A platelayer is a railway worker who lays and maintains the rails, so literally works on the track.

clue.text: Short chap who puts his finger up inside filthy place

indicators.note: inside places one item within the other, so the official goes within the dirty place

parts.note: a pigsty, byword for filth

parts.words: chap who puts his finger up
parts.note: a cricket umpire raises a finger to give a batter out; ump is short for umpire

explanation.surface: A rude little man making an obscene gesture in a squalid dive.
explanation.walkthrough: The raised finger reads as rude; in cricket the umpire raises one finger to signal that a batter is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumpy means short and thick, like a stump, so describes someone or something short.

clue.text: According to Spooner, diver could earn extra

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds of the two words trade places

parts.note: a loon is a diving bird, known in Britain as a diver
could and might both express possibility
swap the opening L and M sounds

explanation.surface: A deep-sea diver might be able to make some extra money.
explanation.walkthrough: The diver is the bird, not a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: To moonlight is to have a second job, often secretly, on top of one's main work, earning extra money.

clue.text: "You're welcome," unlikely after "No thanks"

indicators.note: following the refusal means the improbable word is placed behind it

parts.note: taken as written
ta is informal British for thanks
as in a tall story, one hard to believe

explanation.surface: It is odd to say 'You're welcome' to someone who has just said 'No thanks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Not at all is a polite reply to thanks, meaning the help was no trouble, just like you're welcome.

clue.text: African croc swims among carp

indicators.note: being among things means sitting in their midst, so the shuffled letters go within

parts.note: to carp is to complain or moan

indicators.note: something that swims moves about freely, so these letters move into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An African crocodile swimming through a shoal of carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' is the verb to complain, not the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a North African country, so a Moroccan is a person from Africa, or something African.

clue.text: Sticking-up hair that's unpleasant under hood

indicators.note: in a down entry, a part placed under another follows it

parts.note: a cowl is a monk's hood
ick, an expression of disgust

explanation.surface: Greasy, unruly hair sticking out from under a hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowlick is a tuft of hair growing in a different direction so that it sticks up and will not lie flat.

clue.text: Family on father's side turned brown in time

indicators.note: in places the colour within the period word

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: turned around means the word for brown runs the other way

parts.note: tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: Relatives on the paternal side got suntanned in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnate is a relative descended through the male line, so kin on the father's side.

clue.text: Gulf state prepared with US president dropping round

parts.note: à la, in cookery, means served or prepared in a given style

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so the ring-shaped letter is removed

parts.note: Barack Obama, 44th President
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A southern state readies itself for a presidential visit that skips a round of campaigning.
explanation.walkthrough: Obama's name loses its O; ALA comes from the cookery phrase à la.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf here is the Gulf of Mexico, and Alabama is one of the five American states whose coastline borders it.

clue.text: Nonsensical fellow reassigned aircrews in lounge

indicators.note: in puts the reshuffled crews within the lazing word

parts.note: to loll is to lounge lazily

indicators.note: reassigned means given new places, so these letters are given new positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A daft man shuffles flight crews about in the airport lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' looks like an airport room but is the verb to loll.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll, author of Alice and Jabberwocky, is the great writer of nonsense verse, a nonsense man.

clue.text: Seats on the front and back of garden tree

indicators.note: taken as backing off, the conjunction loses its final letter
placed at the front means the seating word starts the entry

parts.note: a row of seats in a theatre
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seating placed at the front and back of a garden with a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose parse: ROW goes at the front, then 'and' with its back end cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a small tree with red berries widely planted in gardens.

clue.text: Singer sounding like 8?

indicators.note: sounding like signals that the answer is said the same as what follows, not spelt the same

parts.note: 8-down is pronounced like loos, and two loos said together are loo-loo

explanation.surface: A singer whose name sounds like another answer in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: LOSE, the answer to 8, is said like 'loos', the plural of loo (a British toilet); one loo plus another gives LU-LU.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulu is the stage name of a Scottish pop singer famous since the 1960s for Shout.

clue.text: Difficulty meeting once a year, some paper claims

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the paper word grips the meeting

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
Annual General Meeting

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports trouble at a company's annual meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some paper' suggests a newspaper; it is a measure of sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is literally a bog, and figuratively an awkward, complicated situation hard to escape, a difficulty.

clue.text: Irish county town's bar good at all times

indicators.note: bar here means except, so the letter for good is excluded

parts.note: Galway is both a county and its town in the west of Ireland
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A pub in an Irish town that is open round the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub; it means 'except'.
explanation.definitionFit: Always and at all times are straightforward synonyms meaning constantly, on every occasion.

clue.text: Rickshaw takes two Anatolians leaving third behind

parts.note: says the next word is taken twice

indicators.note: leaving behind a thing means abandoning it, so each word abandons its third letter

parts.note: Anatolia is the Asian heartland of Turkey, so two of its people

explanation.surface: A rickshaw ride for two Turkish travellers who leave a third passenger behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Both TURKs drop their third letter, the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuk-tuk is a motorised three-wheeled rickshaw used as a taxi in South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Start at the end of riddle, they teach you

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved to the far end, the rest staying in order

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve for soil or gravel

explanation.surface: Teachers pose a puzzle by beginning at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' is not a puzzle but a gardener's sieve; move its S to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainers are coaches or instructors who teach skills, so they teach you.
